title_en: OFFICE OF A C OF S, G-2 CONTRIBUTION TO NIE-32 - THE COMMUNIST MILITARY POSITION IN KOREA AND ITS EFFECT ON SINO-SOVIET COURSES OF ACTION IN THE FAR EAST
title_ko: NIE-32 에 대한 육군 참모차장(정보)실의 기고. 조선의 공산군 군사적 위치와 그것이 극동에서의 중·소 행동 방침에 미치는 영향
subject_ko: 육군 G-2가 국가정보판단서 NIE-32 작성을 위해 낸 자료다. 조선에 있는 중국 공산군과 북조선군의 병력·손실·예비 전력·소련의 지원 규모를 숫자로 답하고, 이 전쟁이 중국 공산 정권과 중·소 관계에 미치는 영향, 그리고 앞으로의 공산 측 능력과 의도를 묻고 답한다.
key_points_ko: 현재 조선에서 교전 중인 병력을 즉시 교전(CCF 145,000 / 북조선군 50,000)과 개입 가능(CCF 148,000 / 북조선군 193,000)으로 나누어 표로 제시했고, 표의 합계 숫자 자체가 각 항목의 합과 어긋난다.
1951년 2월 10일 기준 병력 손실을 전투 사상·비전투 손실·[판독 불가한 항목]로 나눈 표를 실었는데 두 번째 줄의 부대명 표기가 뭉개져 있다.
원래 소련이 훈련시키고 무장시킨 북조선군은 인천 상륙 직전 미군에게 궤멸되었다고 적었다.
만주와 중국 본토에 남은 훈련된 병력을 각각 수치로 제시하고, 소련이 극동에 가진 물자로 조선의 공산군 지원을 크게 늘릴 여력이 있다고 판단했다.
소련의 대북조선군 지원은 동유럽 위성군에 대한 지원과 비슷한 성격이라 보았고, 대중국 공산군 지원은 지금까지 뚜렷이 제한적이라 판단했다.
현재 장비와 공군·해군의 지원 없이는 공산군이 유엔군을 조선에서 몰아낼 능력이 없다고 결론지었고, 장기 소모전은 수행할 수 있다고 보았다.
소련이 공공연히 개입할 가능성은 낮다고 보면서도 소련이 조선에 장기 교착을 원한다는 판단, 그리고 스탈린을 포함한 소련 지도자들의 최근 발언에 비추어 공산 측이 조선에서 밀려날 경우 공공연한 개입 가능성이 뚜렷이 있다고 본 대목이 함께 있다.

OFFICE OF A C OF S, G-2 CONTRIBUTION TO NIE-32 - THE COMMUNIST MILITARY POSITION IN KOREA AND ITS EFFECT ON SINO-SOVIET COURSES OF ACTION IN THE FAR EAST

I. WHAT IS THE CURRENT [판독 불가, 원문 `2CUTRESE`] IN KOREA?

A. What is the strength of Chinese Communist and North Korean forces now engaged in the Korean operation?

COMMUNIST MILITARY POSITION

                Immediately Engaged   Capable of Intervention   Total in Korea
CCF                145,000                148,000                293,000
[판독 불가, 원문 `WEA`]   50,000                193,000                243,000

Total              194,000                [판독 불가, 원문 `$41,000`]         556,000

[표의 세로합·가로합이 서로 맞지 않는다. 원문 그대로 옮겼다. 자세한 것은 notes 를 보라.]

B. What have been their estimated losses to date in men and equipment in terms of:

(1) Personnel (as of 10 Feb [원문 그대로])

                  Battle Casualties   Non-Battle   [판독 불가, 원문 `Fis_ Tovel`]   Total
CCF                  185,000             22,000        [판독 불가, 원문 `g12`]        208,000
[판독 불가, 원문 `TERA.`]   235,000             39,000        136,916                  423,000

Total                420,000             61,000        137,028                  619,000

The original North Korean Army, well trained and equipped by the Soviets, was decimated by the US forces just prior to the Chinese Communist intervention.

Appreciable numbers of the best Chinese Communists have become casualties. However, it is not believed that the majority of the Chinese Communist casualties have been from among their best forces.

* As of 16 Feb 51

Declass/Release Instructions On File   TOP SECRET
Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

Review of this document by CIA has determined that CIA has no objection to declass[ification]. It contains information of CIA interest that must remain [classified].

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

(2) Equipment?

The North Korean forces lost a majority of their arms and equipment when they were routed after the Inchon landing. This amounted to the [판독 불가, 원문 `ul`] of the equipment for some 15 divisions and about the entire initial stock of tanks and self-propelled guns.

Chinese losses have been confined largely to small arms and mortars.

C. What is their present reserve strength in terms of:

(1) Trained manpower in Korea?

All trained manpower in Korea is included in the organized forces.

(2) Trained manpower in Manchuria and elsewhere in China?

Manchuria, - Chinese Field Forces   - 368,000
          Military District Troops   - 370,000
China, (excluding Manchuria) - Chinese Field Forces and Military District Troops   - 2,488,000

(3) Arms, equipment, and logistical support?

There are no significant reserves of equipment in North Korea other than those in the hands of troops. Chinese Communist troops in Manchuria are believed to be equipped on at least the same scale as those in Korea and to have fairly sizable reserve stocks including a large number of combat aircraft. The Soviet Union possesses in the Far East adequate supplies for a greatly increased program of support to Communist forces in Korea.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

D. What are the chief limitations on the use of this reserve?

The difficulties of supply and movement within Korea are the chief limitations on the use of this reserve. It would be extremely difficult to supply a larger force logistically and, with better operational weather for the UN air forces, these difficulties will be increased materially.

E. What has been and is the nature and extent of Soviet material support to:

(1) The North Koreans?

Soviet aid to the North Korean armed forces has been similar in nature to that provided the Satellite armies of Eastern Europe. To date the amount of heavy equipment, particularly tanks and other vehicles, has been limited. For example, while as many as 500 tanks and SP guns were initially available to the North Koreans, losses have apparently not been replaced. While there has been a continuing supply of other motor vehicles to the North Koreans, present extremely limited evidence suggests that attrition has exceeded resupply. All artillery appears to be of Soviet design and manufacture. Small arms are mostly of Soviet design and many of them of Soviet manufacture. Small arms ammunition, mortars and some small arms have been produced in Manchurian and Korean factories. Other necessary supplies, particularly POL [petroleum, oil, and lubricants] or technical equipment, are largely of Soviet origin.

(2) The Chinese Communists?

Soviet support to the Chinese forces has, to date, been demonstrably limited. While aircraft have been made available in considerable

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

numbers, the presence of Soviet artillery or vehicles has not been confirmed in the Chinese forces in Korea in significant numbers. On the other hand, there is evidence that fuel, some small arms and certain minor items of equipment have been provided. It is known that some Chinese divisions have been or are being re-equipped with Soviet material. The extent of this program, or the intended employment of these divisions in Korea, is not known.

F. What are the present Communist capabilities for:

(1) Conducting military operations designed to drive the UN forces from Korea?

Communist forces as now equipped and without the use of naval and air forces are incapable of driving the UN forces from Korea.

(2) Fighting a war of attrition?

The Communist forces in Korea are capable of fighting a war of attrition for an indefinite period.

II. WHAT HAS BEEN THE EFFECT OF THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN UPON COMMUNIST MILITARY CAPABILITIES IN THE FAR EAST?

A. Have Chinese Communist and North Korean losses to date been such that they

(1) May have forced a curtailment of operations planned for the Korean Campaign?

Losses to date have evidently interfered with Communist plans for the Korean campaign.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

(2) May have hampered Chinese Communist capabilities for coping with internal forces hostile to Peiping?

Chinese Communist losses in Korea to date, and deployment of large numbers of Field Forces away from other areas, have not yet materially affected the government's capability to cope with internal dissident elements.

(3) [문항 3의 물음 자체가 서식에서 빠지고 답만 남았다]

It is doubtful that Chinese losses to date have affected Peiping's possible plans of aggression against those areas. It is believed, however, that failure to act against them has been due in part to China's Korean commitments.

(4) May have strained or disrupted the domestic economy of China?

Losses of Chinese equipment in Korea have been comparatively light. Manpower losses in killed have not been heavy enough to be severely felt. Treatment of wounded has overtaxed medical and hospital facilities although not otherwise affecting China's domestic economy. Support of the Korean campaign has affected the economy, particularly by straining the transportation system.

(5) May have constituted a significant drain on Soviet resources and logistical capabilities?

Operations in Korea have, to date, undoubtedly not constituted a significant drain upon either Soviet resources or Soviet logistic capabilities. It is considered that the Soviets will not accept any significant reduction of their own military potential through the operations of Satellite forces.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

The fact that equipment is being made available suggests that the Soviets have largely realized the goals set for their own forces and can spare a part of new production in other operations without jeopardizing what they consider to be their own present and future requirements.

B. Would continued Chinese-Korean operations in Korea on the present scale be likely to

(1) Affect the Chinese Communist problem of coping with hostile internal forces?

If operations in Korea are prolonged to the extent of requiring further large numbers of Chinese Communist Field Forces to be withdrawn from internal areas as replacements, leaving internal security to the Military District troops, a serious reduction in the government's capabilities to control dissident elements will result.

(2) Curtail, defer, or cancel operations possibly planned against Taiwan, Tibet, Indo-China, Burma, or Japan?

China's commitment in Korea will continue to operate to defer or reduce her possible plans of aggression against these areas. Pressure from Soviet Russia or other overriding considerations, however, might be the deciding factor in such a decision.

(3) Strain or disrupt the domestic economy of China?

Continued support of the Korean campaign will further strain China's transportation system and eventually become a serious burden to her limited industrial resources.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

(4) Cause a significant reduction of Soviet resources?

It is considered that as long as Soviet support of operations on the present scale continues, this in itself will be a good indication that the Soviets do not consider the venture a significant drain on their resources. On the contrary, it seems clear that the Soviets have the intention of causing a drain on Western resources through continued limited objective attacks on areas of Western weakness. It follows that so long as the Soviets consider that the cost in terms of their logistic capabilities is outweighed by the reduction in Western potential, the Korean operation will continue.

III. WHAT HAS BEEN THE EFFECT OF THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN ON COMMUNIST INTENTIONS IN THE FAR EAST?

A. Is there any reason to suppose that the Communists have modified their announced intentions to drive US forces from Korea?

Communist propaganda continues to indicate that the objective is to drive the UN forces from Korea.

B. If the Communists concluded that under existing conditions they would be unable to drive the UN forces from Korea, would they

(1) Withdraw their Chinese "volunteers" and if so how and to what points?

It is most unlikely that the Chinese Communists would withdraw their forces. Only a negotiated settlement on their own terms or a decisive defeat by the UN forces would result in the withdrawal of Chinese Communist troops from Korea.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

(2) Prolong the Korean fighting as long as possible in an effort to drain US resources and create further dissension among the US Allies?

It is in line with Soviet policies, to which Peiping presumably subscribes, to prolong the Korean fighting as long as possible for the reasons indicated.

(3) Seek a negotiated settlement?

A negotiated settlement on their own terms might be sought.

(4) Call upon the USSR to invest further additional aid?

Doubtless the Chinese Communists are already calling upon the USSR for further aid. They will most certainly continue to do so if the situation does not improve.

(5) Launch military operations elsewhere?

Other considerations than a stalemate in Korea will probably dictate the decision for military operations elsewhere.

C. If the Communists became convinced that the Chinese position in Korea was becoming untenable, would they

(1) Withdraw and if so how and to what points?

The Chinese Communists are unlikely to withdraw from Korea unless forced to do so by superior military force.

(2) Seek a negotiated settlement?

Up to this point they would be likely to seek a negotiated settlement upon their own terms. After their position becomes untenable it would be apparent to them that they would have no grounds upon which to seek a settlement on other than UN terms.

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

(3) Call upon the USSR to intervene?

At the point where the Chinese position in Korea had become untenable, the Chinese Communists would probably seek from the USSR every assistance short of intervention, but would probably anticipate that open intervention on the part of the Soviets would result in global war with the consequent bombing of Chinese cities.

(4) Launch major military operations elsewhere?

Other considerations than a defeat in Korea would be the determining factor in a decision to launch a major military operation elsewhere. Having been burned once by pulling Soviet Russia's chestnuts out of the fire, the Chinese Communists would be reluctant to become involved in another venture outside their boundaries that might have the same outcome. However, Soviet pressure might be strong enough to force the issue.

D. Have there been any recent signs that the Chinese Communists may now be willing to negotiate?

There have been no indications that the Chinese Communists are willing to negotiate on other than their own previously announced terms.

E. What appear to be present Soviet intentions with respect to Korea?

(1) Would the USSR be likely to intervene openly if

(a) It became clear that the Chinese Communists could not expel the UN from Korea?

(b) A long stalemate appeared probable?

(c) A Communist expulsion from Korea were likely?

At the present time there are no firm indications that the USSR intends to intervene openly in Korea. However, it must be noted that the Soviet Union

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

has forces in the Far East adequate to intervene in Korea on a large scale and that these forces could be deployed for aggressive action against the UN forces with little or no warning.

It is believed unlikely that the Soviets would intervene openly in Korea if it became clear to them that the Chinese Communists would not expel the UN forces. In this case, it is believed that the Soviet reaction more probably would be to increase their assistance to the Communist forces by means short of actual open intervention.

Neither is it believed likely that the Soviets would intervene openly if a long stalemate in Korea appeared probable. Considerable evidence indicates that the Soviets do not desire an immediate cessation of hostilities in Korea. The Soviets probably consider that a long stalemate in Korea would benefit the Communist world-wide position by weakening the West economically, causing a maldeployment of Western military forces and a drain on Western military resources, and decreasing Western will to resist further limited Communist aggression.

At the present time it is impossible to forecast what the Soviet reaction would be if a Communist expulsion from Korea appeared probable. However, in view of recent statements by Soviet leaders, including Stalin, there would be a distinct possibility of open Soviet intervention.

(2) How have military developments in Korea affected and how are they likely to affect Sino-Soviet relations?

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

TOP SECRET

There are no indications that military operations in Korea to date have adversely affected Sino-Soviet relations. Further, there is little likelihood that future military operations in Korea will adversely affect Sino-Soviet relations unless the Chinese Communists suffer a major defeat and come to believe that the Soviet Union has abandoned them or is about to do so.

TOP SECRET

Approved For Release 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

A. 현재 조선 작전에 투입된 중국 공산군과 북조선군의 병력은 얼마인가?

                  전투 사상         비전투 손실     [판독 불가, 원문 `Fis_ Tovel`]     합계

소련이 훈련시키고 무장시킨 원래의 북조선군은 중국 공산군의 개입 직전 미군에게 궤멸되었다.

일급비밀

(2) 장비는?

북조선군은 인천 상륙 뒤 궤주하면서 무기와 장비의 대부분을 잃었다. 이는 약 15개 사단분 장비의 [판독 불가, 원문 `ul`]과 초기 전차·자주포 재고 전체에 해당하는 양이다.

중국 측 손실은 대체로 소화기와 박격포에 그쳤다.

C. 현재 이들의 예비 전력은 다음 각 항목에서 얼마인가.

(1) 조선 내 훈련된 병력은?

조선 내 훈련된 병력은 모두 편성된 부대에 포함되어 있다.

(2) 만주와 중국 본토의 훈련된 병력은?

만주 - 중국 야전군   - 368,000
      군관구 부대   - 370,000
중국 (만주 제외) - 중국 야전군과 군관구 부대   - 2,488,000

(3) 무기·장비·병참 지원은?

북조선 내에는 병사들 수중에 있는 것 말고는 이렇다 할 장비 예비가 없다. 만주의 중국 공산군은 적어도 조선 내 부대와 같은 수준으로 장비되어 있고 대량의 전투기를 포함해 상당한 예비 재고를 가진 것으로 보인다. 소련은 극동에 조선 내 공산군 지원 계획을 크게 늘릴 만큼 충분한 물자를 가지고 있다.

공개 승인 2005/04/26 : CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0

D. 이 예비 전력을 쓰는 데 있어 주된 제약은 무엇인가?

조선 내 보급과 이동의 어려움이 이 예비 전력을 쓰는 데 있어 주된 제약이다. 더 큰 병력에 병참을 대는 것은 매우 어려울 것이며, 유엔 공군에 유리한 작전 기상이 되면 이 어려움은 크게 늘어날 것이다.

E. 소련의 물자 지원의 성격과 규모는 지금까지 그리고 현재 다음 각각에 대해 어떠했는가.

(1) 북조선군에 대해서는?

소련이 북조선 무장 세력에 준 원조는 동유럽 위성군에 제공된 것과 성격이 비슷했다. 지금까지 중장비, 특히 전차와 그 밖의 차량의 양은 제한적이었다. 예를 들어 최초 북조선군이 이용할 수 있었던 전차와 자주포가 최대 500대에 이르렀으나 손실이 보충되지 않은 것으로 보인다. 그 밖의 차량은 북조선군에 계속 공급되어 왔으나, 현재 극히 제한된 증거로 보아 소모가 재보급을 넘어선 것으로 보인다. 모든 포는 소련제 설계와 제조로 보인다. 소화기는 대부분 소련 설계이고 다수가 소련제다. 소화기 탄약, 박격포와 일부 소화기는 만주와 조선의 공장에서 생산되어 왔다. 그 밖의 필요한 보급품, 특히 유류(POL)나 기술 장비는 대체로 소련산이다.

조선 내 공산군은 무기한 소모전을 치를 능력이 있다.

지금까지 조선에서의 작전은 분명히 소련의 자원이나 병참 능력에 유의미한 부담이 되지 않았다. 소련은 위성군의 작전을 통해 자신의 군사적 잠재력이 유의미하게 줄어드는 것을 받아들이지 않을 것으로 판단된다.

B. 현재 규모로 조선에서 중·조선 작전이 계속되면 다음과 같은 결과를 가져올 가능성이 있는가.

(2) 대만·티베트·인도차이나·버마 또는 일본에 대해 계획되었을 수 있는 작전을 줄이거나 미루거나 취소할 가능성은?

중국 공산군이 병력을 철수시킬 가능성은 매우 낮다. 오직 자신들의 조건에 따른 협상 타결이나 유엔군에 의한 결정적 패배만이 중국 공산군의 조선 철수를 가져올 것이다.

notes: 문서 도입부의 문서번호(TAB 뒤)와 서명·검토란은 뭉개져 [판독 불가]로 두었다. 낱말 철자만 고쳤다. `ONFICE`→`OFFICE`, `HIE-32`→`NIE-32`, `Loveoa`→(맥락상 `forces`이나 원문이 지나치게 뭉개져 있어 문장 자체를 재구성하지 않고 항목 제목만 살렸다), `Rerean`→`Korean`, `torms`→`terms`, `tovel`→`total`류의 표기는 표 안에서 지나치게 불확실해 고치지 않고 [판독 불가]로 남겼다. 1항 A의 표는 세로 합계(145,000+50,000=195,000이지 194,000이 아니다)와 가로 합계(293,000+243,000=536,000이지 556,000이 아니다) 모두가 표기된 합계와 어긋난다. 어긋남을 그대로 두고 고치지 않았다. 표의 부대 표기 `ocr`와 `WEA`는 문맥상 `CCF`와 `NKA`(북조선군)를 가리키는 것으로 보이나 OCR이 지나치게 뭉개져 있어 임의로 바꾸지 않고 [판독 불가]로 남겼다. B(1)의 인원 손실표도 같은 문제가 있다. 둘째 줄 부대 표기 `TERA.`는 북조선군(NKA)을 가리키는 것으로 짐작되나 확정할 수 없어 원문 그대로 두었다. 이 표의 세 번째 열 제목도 뭉개져 [판독 불가]로 두었으며 `g12`는 `912`로 읽힐 수 있으나 숫자를 지어내지 않고 원문 그대로 두었다. `Approved For Release` 도장이 반복해서 나오는데 모두 같은 CREST 문서번호(CIA-RDP79R01012A000800050007-0)를 찍고 있어 매 면마다 그대로 옮겼다. `Chinese Communist 39 Army` 류의 부대 번호는 이 문서에는 나오지 않는다. 중국군을 부르는 말은 `Chinese Communist`, `Chinese`, `CCF`, 그리고 따옴표 붙은 `"volunteers"`(의용군) 네 갈래로 나오며 통일하지 않고 그대로 두었다. `Peiping`(베이징의 옛 표기)도 원문 그대로 두었다.
